name: manual_aedbe2
claim: Never judge a config value 'stale' or 'correct' relative to an upstream/grandmother repo from memory or from your own fork's history alone — fetch the live upstream file (raw.githubusercontent.com or equivalent) directly before asserting what it currently contains

decisions.notes: Mid-investigation, I initially concluded periscope's .golangci.nilaway.yml include-pkgs value (go.kenn.io/agentsview) was 'stale' relative to a supposedly-renamed module path (github.com/latentsignal-org/periscope), and 'fixed' it to match. That fix was backwards: the module rename itself was the unauthorized change (see lesson_0c339d39a80c). Only after directly curling kenn-io/agentsview's live go.mod and latentsignal-org/periscope's live go.mod (both still go.kenn.io/agentsview and github.com/wesm/agentsview respectively -- neither ever adopted the invented path) did the true state become clear. Git blame/log --follow on the actual rename commit, plus live upstream fetches, are the only reliable ground truth -- not assumptions built on a prior (also-wrong) conclusion from earlier in the same session.
